trickyParts: The plan's 'a deployment that configures no issuer exchanges nothing' is false: the access-token subject type is always registered (ExchangeConfig.tokenTypes) and Set.Machine needs no entry, so a machine login's token still exchanges. The docs say that, and the production negative control shows the type registered.

The plan said the pod's bearer goes into a 'generation Secret'; the code puts it in each launch's secrets, which travel in the generation's start command and the launcher writes into g<generation>. The docs follow the code.

The operator-launched controller presents controller.yaml's own dispatch_token_file (controllerEnvironment), not the daemon's bearer; the docs say so, and subsection A distinguishes the daemon-launched controller.

An embedded Postgres 16.4 (zonky jar) is left unpacked and stopped at $TMPDIR/pg; start it with LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$TMPDIR/pg/lib $TMPDIR/pg/bin/pg_ctl -D $TMPDIR/pg/data -o "-p 54329 -k $TMPDIR/pg -c listen_addresses=127.0.0.1" -l $TMPDIR/pg/pg.log start. The proof's dev-broker copy and exchange client are at $TMPDIR/infra228/dev-broker-proof.sh and $TMPDIR/infra228/exchange_proof.py.
Comparing two roles' credentials needs a second container: the architect ran the salted-digest comparison, since a role cannot read another role's private directory.

main (14d907b6 and later) runs a pod's roles in one `roles` container with per-role namespaces, so the pod paragraph now says the broker's token is projected 'for a role', not 'into a role container'. The rest of the paragraph's facts (secrets[dispatchTokenKey] in prepare, the launcher writing g<generation>) were re-checked on main and hold.
check-ci-filters.sh imports pyyaml, which the pod lacks; a uv venv at $TMPDIR/ciflt with pyyaml==6.0.3 put first on PATH runs the script unmodified.

The fence calls the unexported (*Provider).decide with a Provider holding only the exchange policy and a Kubernetes issuer config with nil Keys: decide checks a pod token's audience and never resolves a key.
